title: Geography: Around the World / Science: Principles and Discoveries

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.hint: It is the world's largest metropolitan area by many measures.
questions.explanation: Tokyo is Japan's capital.

questions.prompt: The Sahara Desert is located on which continent?
questions.hint: It spans much of the continent's north.
questions.explanation: The Sahara is in North Africa.

questions.prompt: The Amazon River flows mainly across which continent?
questions.hint: Much of its basin lies in Brazil.
questions.explanation: The Amazon is South America's largest river system.

questions.prompt: The Alps are primarily located on which continent?
questions.hint: They cross countries including Switzerland and Austria.
questions.explanation: The Alps are a major European mountain range.

questions.prompt: The Mekong River flows through which broad region?
questions.hint: It passes Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam.
questions.explanation: The Mekong is one of Southeast Asia's major rivers.

questions.prompt: The Bering Strait separates Asia from which continent?
questions.hint: Russia and Alaska face one another across it.
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait separates northeastern Asia from Alaska.

questions.prompt: Which country has more natural lakes than any other?
questions.hint: A large share of the world's lakes lie there.
questions.explanation: Canada contains more lakes than any other country.

questions.prompt: The Bosporus runs through which city?
questions.hint: It separates the city's European and Asian sides.
questions.explanation: The Bosporus passes through Istanbul.

questions.prompt: The Pannonian Basin lies mainly in which part of Europe?
questions.hint: Hungary occupies much of it.
questions.explanation: The Pannonian Basin is centered on Hungary in Central Europe.

questions.prompt: Timor-Leste occupies part of which island?
questions.hint: The country shares the island with Indonesia.
questions.explanation: Timor-Leste lies on the eastern part of Timor.

questions.prompt: San Marino is an enclave within which country?
questions.hint: It lies near the Adriatic side of the Apennines.
questions.explanation: San Marino is surrounded by Italy.

questions.prompt: Which river flows out of Lake Victoria and becomes part of the Nile system?
questions.hint: It travels north through Uganda and South Sudan.
questions.explanation: The White Nile flows from the Lake Victoria region.

questions.prompt: The Khyber Pass links Afghanistan with which country?
questions.hint: It has long connected Central and South Asia.
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass crosses the Afghanistan-Pakistan frontier.

questions.prompt: The Fergana Valley is shared mainly by Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and which country?
questions.hint: It is one of Central Asia's most densely populated regions.
questions.explanation: The Fergana Valley extends into Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.

questions.prompt: Cabinda is an exclave of which African country?
questions.hint: It is separated from the rest of the country by a strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
questions.explanation: Cabinda is an Angolan exclave on the Atlantic coast.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.hint: Plants use its carbon to build sugars.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis consumes carbon dioxide and water.

questions.prompt: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at what Celsius temperature?
questions.hint: The Fahrenheit value is 212.
questions.explanation: At sea-level pressure, pure water boils at 100°C.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes are normally found in a human somatic cell?
questions.hint: They occur in 23 pairs.
questions.explanation: Most human body cells contain 46 chromosomes.

questions.prompt: What electric charge does an electron carry?
questions.hint: A proton has the opposite sign.
questions.explanation: Electrons carry negative elementary charge.

questions.prompt: Which travels faster in a vacuum: light or sound?
questions.hint: Sound requires a material medium.
questions.explanation: Light travels through vacuum; sound does not.

questions.prompt: An element's atomic number equals its number of what?
questions.hint: This number defines the element.
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.prompt: What is osmosis?

choices.text: Movement of solvent across a selectively permeable membrane

questions.hint: Water commonly moves toward the side with more dissolved solute.
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of solvent through a semipermeable membrane.

questions.prompt: A catalyst speeds a reaction mainly by lowering what?
questions.hint: It provides an alternative reaction pathway.
questions.explanation: Catalysts lower activation energy without being consumed overall.

questions.prompt: Which cellular structure synthesizes proteins?
questions.hint: It reads messenger RNA.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides.

questions.prompt: The Doppler effect is a change in observed frequency caused by what?
questions.hint: A passing siren changes pitch.
questions.explanation: Relative motion between source and observer produces a Doppler shift.

questions.prompt: In thermodynamics, entropy is most closely associated with what?

choices.text: The number of accessible microscopic arrangements

questions.hint: More possible microstates generally means more entropy.
questions.explanation: Statistical entropy measures the multiplicity of microstates compatible with a macrostate.

questions.prompt: Telomeres are structures found at what location?
questions.hint: They help protect chromosomes during replication.
questions.explanation: Telomeres are repetitive DNA-protein structures at chromosome ends.

questions.prompt: A p-value is calculated under the assumption that what is true?

choices.text: The alternative hypothesis is certainly true

questions.hint: It measures how surprising the data are under a reference model.
questions.explanation: A p-value is the probability, under the null model, of results at least as extreme as observed.

questions.prompt: At constant temperature and pressure, a process is thermodynamically spontaneous when the change in Gibbs free energy is what?
questions.hint: The symbol ΔG should fall below zero.
questions.explanation: A negative ΔG indicates thermodynamic favorability at constant temperature and pressure.

questions.prompt: In quantum field theory, renormalization chiefly addresses how physical predictions depend on what?
questions.hint: Measured parameters can vary with energy scale.
questions.explanation: Renormalization absorbs divergences into scale-dependent physical parameters.
